'''Chaim Sukenik''' (born May 1951) is an American-Israeli chemist and academic administrator. He is a professor emeritus of chemistry at [[Bar-Ilan University]] and served as the president of the [[Jerusalem College of Technology]] (JCT) from 2013 to 2025.<ref name="JCT_Bio">{{cite web |title=JCT Admins - Jerusalem College of Technology |url=https://www.jct.ac.il/en/jct-admins/ |website=Jerusalem College of Technology |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref> Sukenik is widely recognized for his research in [[nanotechnology]], surface chemistry, and materials science, particularly the development of [[self-assembled monolayers]] (SAMs).

== Early life and education ==
Sukenik was born and raised in the United States. He attended [[Yeshiva University]], graduating [[magna cum laude]] in 1972 with a Bachelor of Arts in chemistry.<ref name="BIU_Profile">{{cite web |title=Prof. Chaim Sukenik - Department of Chemistry |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/sukenik |website=Bar-Ilan University |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref> 

He completed his doctoral studies at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech), earning his [[Ph.D.]] in 1976 under the supervision of [[Robert G. Bergman]]. His dissertation focused on the catalysis of organic reactions and molecular orientation within crystals.<ref name="Caltech_Thesis">{{cite web |title=Sukenik, Chaim N. (1976) Catalysis of organic reactions |url=https://thesis.caltech.edu/10060/ |website=Caltech Thesis Archive |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref> He subsequently held a [[National Science Foundation]] postdoctoral fellowship at [[UCLA]] working with Orville L. Chapman.<ref name="BIU_Profile"/>

== Academic career ==
Sukenik served as a faculty member at [[Case Western Reserve University]] from 1977 to 1995, where his research focused on interfacial chemistry and synthetic organic chemistry.<ref name="BIU_Profile"/>

In 1995, Sukenik immigrated to Israel and joined the faculty of [[Bar-Ilan University]] (BIU). He held the Edward and Judy Steinberg Chair in Nanotechnology and served as the head of the Department of Chemistry and the dean of the Faculty of Exact Sciences.<ref name="JCT_Announce">{{cite web |title=Bar-Ilan Professor Chaim Sukenik Elected President of the Jerusalem College of Technology |url=https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=33&type=1&news=2037 |website=Bar-Ilan University News |date=May 28, 2013 |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref> He was the founding director of the Bar-Ilan Institute for Nanotechnology and Advanced Materials (BINA).<ref name="BINA">{{cite web |title=BINA Leadership History |url=https://nano.biu.ac.il/ |website=Bar-Ilan Institute for Nanotechnology |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>

In 2013, Sukenik was elected president of the [[Jerusalem College of Technology]]. During his tenure, the college significantly expanded its engineering and health science programs, particularly for the [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi]] and religious sectors in Israel.<ref name="JCT_Expansion">{{cite web |title=JCT President Tours US to Build Momentum for International Program |url=https://www.jns.org/wire/jerusalem-college-of-technology-president-tours-us-to-build-momentum-for-international-program-future-womens-campus/ |website=JNS |date=April 11, 2022 |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==
Sukenik's research is centered on surface modification and the chemical properties of thin films. He is a pioneer in the use of [[self-assembled monolayers]] (SAMs) to control the physical and chemical properties of surfaces at the molecular level. 

His work has practical applications in:
* Microelectronics: Developing oxide thin films and interfacial layers for semiconductors.<ref name="Scholar">{{cite web |title=Chaim Sukenik - Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=U2fliSwAAAAJ&hl=en |website=Google Scholar |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>
* Aerospace: Designing protective coatings for satellite materials to withstand the harsh environment of low Earth orbit.<ref name="BIRAD">{{cite web |title=Surface Chemistry and Nano-Coatings |url=https://birad.biz/technologies/surface-chemistry-and-nano-coatings/ |website=BIRAD - Bar-Ilan Research & Development |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>
* Biomedical Engineering: Creating anti-bacterial coatings for medical devices and catheters to prevent biofouling.<ref name="BIRAD"/>

== Awards and recognition ==
* '''Influential Olim Recognition (2014):''' Named by the Israeli Ministry of Aliyah and Integration as one of the most influential immigrants to Israel in the fields of science and medicine over the previous 25 years.<ref name="Chabad_Olim">{{cite web |title=Profiles in Aliyah: Prof. Chaim Sukenik |url=https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/2619472/jewish/Prof-Chaim-Sukenik.htm |website=Chabad.org |access-date=January 28, 2026}}</ref>
* '''Rector’s Prize for Excellence in Research:''' Awarded by Bar-Ilan University for his contributions to the field of chemistry and nanotechnology.<ref name="BIU_Profile"/>
* '''Steinberg Chair in Nanotechnology:''' Appointed to this prestigious endowed chair at Bar-Ilan University in recognition of his leadership in the field.<ref name="JCT_Announce"/>
* '''Phi Beta Kappa:''' Inducted as a member of the academic honor society during his undergraduate studies at Yeshiva University.<ref name="BIU_Profile"/>
